subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw enforce MEMORY.md bootstrap budget limits at save time, or keep truncation handling as warning/diagnostic-only?
rationale: Current main already warns when injected context is truncated, but the remaining request changes user save behavior and may mutate or reject workspace memory files, which is a product policy decision rather than a strict bug fix.

options.title: Add guarded save-time UX
options.body: Add a Control UI budget indicator plus warning/error states, with any hard block and archive action gated by explicit user confirmation and tests for fresh and existing workspaces.

options.title: Keep diagnostics-only
options.body: Close or narrow this issue if maintainers decide `/context`, doctor, docs, and prompt warnings are the intended boundary for bootstrap truncation handling.

options.title: Adapt the diagnostics PR separately
options.body: Close or replace the open fork PR if maintainers only want better `/status` or edit-failure hints without save-time enforcement.

recommendation.title: Add guarded save-time UX
recommendation.body: Add a Control UI budget indicator plus warning/error states, with any hard block and archive action gated by explicit user confirmation and tests for fresh and existing workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Ayaan's recent commit owns the current budget analyzer, diagnostics, and Control UI file-edit surfaces most likely to be touched by this decision.
